A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the outage performance of all schemes is always dominated by the source-to-relays link.
the optimal selection scheme is the one which exploits the instantaneous knowledge of both the source-to-destination as well as the relay-to-destination link.

all of the proposed transmit antenna selection schemes achieve a diversity order that equals the number of available antennas at the source node and that the outage performance of the schemes is dominated by the channel between the source and the destination node, i.e., the channel between the relay and the source node does not have any impact.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal scheme is based on the csi of the source-to-destination link only, while all other schemes require csi on both links.
, depending on the kind of channel state information available to the transmitter, different schemes can be optimal in terms of the outage probability.
, in contrast to conventional single-hop systems, transmit antenna selection for cooperative systems requires always the knowledge of the channel between source and relay.
